next_authority.question: Is the C5A pooled signed-flux blocker a genuine BC1 dynamic-boundary closure floor, a time-integration floor, or primarily a cross-history aggregation/cancellation property of R2?

scientific_interpretation: C5A completes the matched material-by-lower-boundary interaction cell. Unlike B01 C4Z, no reduced B14 lower-zone LARE member crosses the full frozen R2-relative dynamic-groundwater vector.
The negative decision is caused by exactly one frozen component for every lower-zone ladder member: pooled absolute mean signed bottom-flux error.
On the other seven groundwater-vector components, every lower-zone ladder member is no worse than R2. R2 itself has 832 sign mismatches and reversal-sequence mismatches in three of four histories.

R2 obtains an unusually small pooled signed-bias magnitude through strong cancellation among history-specific signed errors; its mean absolute history bias is about three orders of magnitude larger than its pooled bias.
The lower-zone LARE response converges to an apparent floor by R5-R8: R5, R6, R8, R12 and R16 are effectively identical on the blocking signed-bias metric and bottom-flux RMSE.
Consequently the C5A result does not support the interpretation that simply adding more lower-zone state resolves the B14 dynamic-head discrepancy.
Placement evidence nevertheless transfers: R4 remains componentwise no worse than U4 and R8 remains componentwise no worse than U8.
C5A retains its preregistered negative decision. The post-result diagnostic does not change the acceptance vector or create a new frontier.
